text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Two government ministries have complained about dumping of industrial waste off the coast of Ba Ria-Vung Tau by Vedan-Vietnam, a Taiwanese manufacturer of monosodium glutamate based in Dong Nai province.
-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment has revoked the licences of three major joint ventures in the hotel and tourism sector with total pledged investment amounting to more than $612 million.
-- The Vietnam Interpol Office in Hanoi has warned Vietnamese enterprises about the money laudering tricks of international crime organisations through loan offers.
-- Vietnam invested $98.6 million in irrigation systems in 1996.

-- Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, in a letter to the Vietnamese people ahead of his official visit to the country, said he saw more opportunities for cooperation between Vietnam and Japan in the coming years.

-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi told France's ambassador to Vietnam that he hopes the French government will continue to increase its investment in Vietnam and help the country expand its relations with European countries.

-- The chairman of the Hanoi People's Committee, Hoang Van Nghien, has assured the visiting president of South Korea's Daewoo Corporation that Hanoi will create the most favourable conditions it can for investors.
-- The Minister of Culture and Information Nguyen Khoa Diem has launched a campaign to tighten control over publications ahead of the lunar new year holiday, Tet.
